speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, when exactly did you first notice the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive weakness and significant weight loss, have you noticed any weakness in your legs, difficulty speaking, or trouble swallowing? I also need to know if you have experienced any muscle twitching or cramps in the affected arm.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive motor weakness, sensory changes, and significant weight loss is concerning for a compressive lesion or malignancy. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the cervical spine and brain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, we must look for systemic causes. Do you have any other neurological symptoms like double vision, drooping eyelids, or slurred speech, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder function?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and steroid use, do you experience similar weakness or numbness in your legs or other limbs? I also need to know if you have any muscle wasting or atrophy visible in the right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the focal nature of your symptoms and significant weight loss, I need to rule out a peripheral nerve issue or a mass elsewhere. REQUEST TEST: Nerve conduction study and EMG of the right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal MRI and EMG results, I suspect a systemic metabolic or toxic cause given your heavy steroid and alcohol use. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive metabolic panel and liver function tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal workup so far, I need to rule out a functional or psychogenic cause, especially with your history of steroid use. Do you have any other symptoms like fatigue, anxiety, or depression, and have you noticed any tremors or involuntary movements in your right arm?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive weakness, pain, and significant weight loss in the context of steroid use, I suspect an infiltrative process like amyloidosis. REQUEST TEST: Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation.
